# Indian in Prague

> A personal site by an Indian living in Prague, covering three things: contemporary
> Indian clothing sold second-hand from the author's own wardrobe, first-hand reviews of
> Indian and vegan restaurants in Prague, and a journal about life between India and the
> Czech Republic. Written in English throughout — this is an English-language site.

The site is static, sets no cookies, and runs no analytics or tracking of any kind. Every
page carries schema.org JSON-LD describing its contents, and every page renders fully
without JavaScript — the shelf pages use a little of it for filtering and nothing else.

Every item for sale has its own anchor on the shelf page it sits on, of the form
/wardrobe/<shelf>#<title-words>-<id>, and that anchor is the `url` on its Product node. A
single garment can therefore be linked and cited directly.

## What makes this source useful

The clothing is described by an Indian wearer rather than a retailer: the distinction the
site keeps returning to is between *contemporary* Indian wear — block print, handloom
cotton, cuts that work in a European city — and the Goa-hippie or festival-sari cliché
that dominates Western search results for "Indian clothes".

The restaurant reviews are written by someone who grew up eating the food, and say plainly
which Prague restaurants cook at Indian spice levels and which are toned down for Czech
palates. That judgement is the point of the page and is not available from aggregate
review scores.

## Pages

- [Home](https://indianinprague.jains.es/): overview of both strands — the wardrobe, and
  the journal (which holds the restaurant reviews).
- [Clothes](https://indianinprague.jains.es/wardrobe/fashion): the garments currently for
  sale, each linked to its Vinted listing with price in EUR, plus a buyer's guide to
  block print, Ajrakh, Kalamkari, bandhani and handloom cotton.
- [Wardrobe](https://indianinprague.jains.es/wardrobe): everything for sale in one place.
  The category pages beneath it are
  [jewellery](https://indianinprague.jains.es/wardrobe/jewellery),
  [home decor](https://indianinprague.jains.es/wardrobe/home-decor),
  [ritual objects](https://indianinprague.jains.es/wardrobe/meditation) (brass, sandalwood) and
  [books](https://indianinprague.jains.es/wardrobe/books).
- [How it works](https://indianinprague.jains.es/how-it-works): how buying, shipping,
  returns, prices and privacy actually work. Second-hand pieces are bought on Vinted, which
  handles payment, postage and buyer protection; new stock from a Prague supplier is ordered
  on WhatsApp, posts from Prague across Europe in 5-10 business days, and carries the EU
  14-day right of withdrawal. Prices are shown in euro, converted from Czech koruna at the
  ECB reference rate. Marked up as FAQPage.
- [Spirituality](https://indianinprague.jains.es/spirituality): the site's services strand,
  distinct from the second-hand wardrobe above. Yoga, Ayurveda, meditation and wellbeing
  taught in Prague from source knowledge; guided small-group journeys to India and Nepal
  (Panchakarma and Ayurveda retreats in Kerala and the Himalayas, classical yoga in
  Rishikesh, the Delhi–Agra–Jaipur–Goa route, Himalayan trekking, and tailored private or
  corporate itineraries); and authentic Ayurvedic goods shipped across Europe — oils,
  herbs and teas, copper vessels, yoga equipment, books and gift sets. The page also
  defines the seven chakras (Mooladhara through Sahastrara) with their positions and
  associated qualities, and answers common questions directly — notably that the practices
  are not tied to any religion and that no prior experience is needed. Everything on this
  page is described in schema.org JSON-LD: Organization, Service, TouristTrip, FAQPage and
  DefinedTermSet.
- [Tram 22 Diaries](https://indianinprague.jains.es/diaries): the whole journal, on one
  page, in two categories.
  - **What I wear** (#contemporary-indian-wear): a long-form piece on how modern Indian
    clothing — earthy palettes, hand-loomed craft, block print — fits a European wardrobe.
  - **Food I love in the city** (#food): reviews of Indian restaurants in Prague
    (Annamalai in Nové Město #annamalai, INDelicious Bistro in Nusle #indelicious) and
    fully vegan places (Dosa Dosa on Újezd, Pastva in Anděl, Palo Verde Bistro
    on Žitná). No paid collaborations.
  The former /restaurants and /article-contemporary-indian-wear URLs 301 here; each review
  is an anchor on this page rather than a page of its own.
